title: Finite scalar domains for closed exceptional localization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite extensions, $m,n\ge1$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, $B=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^n$, and $\varphi:A	o B$ any unital map [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each scheme $T$ use constant module sheaves on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and write $S_T^{A,B}K=K_B=K\otimes_A^LB$ for uncompleted derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The notation $D^b_{ctf}$ means bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$; all scheme maps are $k$-maps [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the constructible exceptional functors and their adjunctions on bounded constructible inputs of etale origin [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and ordinary derived direct images [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, with $a\le b$, $K_B\in D^b_{ctf}(T,B)$ has Tor amplitude in the same interval. More precisely, for the site comparison $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], there is a bounded flat constructible etale $A$-complex $Q$, zero outside $[a,b]$, with $
u_T^*Q\cong K$ and a $B$-linear identification $
u_T^*(Q\otimes_A B)\cong K_B$. Its scalar-extended terms are flat constructible $B$-modules.

For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, put $N_A=Ri_A^!M$ and $N_B=Ri_B^!M_B$. Choose a finite affine chart family for $i$ as in [thm-sf-preservation-class], put $D=\max d_U$ and $e=\dim X$, with $D=e=0$ on empty relevant families or schemes. Then $N_A$, $(N_A)_B$, and $N_B$ are bounded constructible of Tor amplitude in $[a-2D,b+2e+1]$ over their respective coefficient rings. Each bounded constructible complex just mentioned admits a bounded constructible etale origin with the same Tor interval. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

proof.text: Translate intrinsic bounded constructibility to the fixed-scalar etale-origin property using the proved intrinsic_bc_realization_iff helper of FiniteCompactSupportConstructibility, whose proof applies [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Its etale_bc_iff helper translates the finite-stratification constructibility convention using [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison]. Translate intrinsic Tor amplitude by [lem-exc-intrinsic-tor-amplitude-transport]; the source-library torAmplitudeIn_of_mapDerivedCategory reflects the same interval to the etale origin. Finite type over the field makes T Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [lem-sp-etale-scalar-flat-model] to the etale origin and the lifted coefficient homomorphism: obtain Q with flat constructible terms, zero outside [a,b], and its A-linear representing isomorphism, together with all scalar-extended model properties.

Use the already proved pbcComparisonReduction of [def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility], inverted at the etale origin and followed by scalar extension of its isomorphism to K. This yields the B-linear identification of the comparison pullback of the derived etale extension with K_B, for an arbitrary coefficient map. Compose it with comparison pullback of the model isomorphism furnished by [lem-sp-etale-scalar-flat-model] to obtain the required displayed identification for Q tensor B. The same theorem gives bounded constructibility and Tor amplitude [a,b] over B. Source-library comparisonUpperStar bounded-constructibility preservation and torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory give their fixed-scalar pro-etale versions. Transport along the B-linear isomorphism, then use the intrinsic constructibility and Tor bridges from Step 1. For the etale origin required by ClosedScalarDomain, extract any origin from fixed-scalar bounded constructibility and reflect the Tor interval. This proves the scalar assertion and the private closedScalar_fixed_domain helper.

Translate the input finite-Tor constructibility and Tor interval to the fixed-scalar predicates by Step 1. Apply clauses (2) and (3) of [thm-sf-preservation-class] to i and the supplied chart family C over E. Its exceptional functor unfolds to the same composite as sfFiniteExceptionalFixed; proof-valued compactification instances agree by proof irrelevance. The private closedScalar_fixed_domain helper gives the asserted intrinsic domain and an etale origin for N_A in I=[a-2*C.maxDimension,b+2*sfDimension X+1]. This interval is ordered by a<=b and nonnegativity of the two natural numbers. Apply the scalar assertion on Z to N_A, obtaining the domain for (N_A)_B. Apply the scalar assertion on X to M, then repeat preservation and the domain helper over L, with exactly the same i and C, obtaining the domain for N_B. This argument includes empty schemes and empty chart families without extra hypotheses.
